legal.privacyDescription: How dj-digger uses optional analytics and cookies, how long choices last, and how to withdraw consent.
legal.termsDescription: Read the terms for using the dj-digger website, its software downloads, music examples and artwork.
legal.bannerText: With your permission, Google Analytics counts visits, installer clicks, Linux command copies and clicks on links to the extension, GitHub and product pages in guides. You can use the whole site if you decline and change your choice in the footer.

controller.heading: Who runs this site?
controller.body: Filip Białogrecki runs dj-digger as a hobby project in Poland and is the controller of personal data collected through this website. For questions or to exercise your rights, email him at the address below. The desktop app and browser extension have their own privacy notice.

hosting.heading: Delivering and securing the site
hosting.body: Google Ireland Limited provides Firebase Hosting. It receives the IP address and technical details of each request to deliver pages and detect abuse. The legal basis is my legitimate interest in providing a reliable and secure website (GDPR Article 6(1)(f)). Firebase retains hosting IP data for a few months.

analytics.heading: Optional visitor statistics
analytics.body: Only with your consent (Article 6(1)(a)) does Google Ireland Limited receive GA4 data such as the page visited, browser and device information, referring site, installer clicks, copies of the Linux install command and a pseudonymous browser identifier. I use this to understand how visitors use the site. The _ga and _ga_* cookies last up to 180 days; subsequent visits do not renew their expiry. The retention setting for user- and event-level data is two months. Standard aggregated reports are separate and can cover longer periods. It also counts visits from guides to product pages and clicks on the extension store and project repository links.

settings.heading: Your browser choices
settings.body: Your browser stores the language and theme you expressly choose until you clear or change them. It remembers an acceptance or refusal of analytics for six calendar months. You can withdraw consent at any time in Cookie settings in the footer. Withdrawal stops future collection and does not affect the lawfulness of earlier processing. You can browse without consenting. These records are necessary to apply your choices. I rely on my legitimate interest in respecting and remembering them (Article 6(1)(f)).

email.heading: Email
email.body: If you write to me, Google Ireland Limited processes your email address, message and any attachments through Gmail. My legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(f)) are responding to your request and, where necessary, establishing or defending claims. I keep correspondence until your request is resolved, and only as long afterwards as a relevant claim requires. Providing contact details is voluntary; I need a return address to reply.

transfers.heading: External links and international transfers
transfers.body: Following a GitHub link connects your browser to GitHub, which receives your IP address and request details under its own privacy statement. Google and GitHub may process data outside the EEA, including in the US. Where applicable, transfers rely on the EU–US Data Privacy Framework for certified recipients or on the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses. The providers describe their safeguards below; you can also ask me for a copy.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.body: You may request access, correction, erasure or restriction, object to processing based on legitimate interests and request portability where applicable. You may complain to the Polish supervisory authority (UODO) or the authority where you live, work or believe an infringement occurred. This site makes no automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

project.heading: Using the project
project.body: Filip Białogrecki maintains this hobby project in Poland. This website provides documentation, demonstrations and links to software downloads. For support, corrections or a rights concern, use the email address below. The site works in a modern web browser over HTTPS. Downloads also work with JavaScript turned off. The download page lists the operating system and architecture for each installer.

software.heading: Software and third-party services
software.body: The project software is available under the Apache License 2.0, including its conditions on redistribution, notices, warranties and liability. Dependencies, fonts and icons retain their respective licences. Use sources, stores and downloads only as their terms and applicable rights permit. You are responsible for confirming purchases and for having permission to use the music.

music.heading: Music and artwork
music.body: The screenshots feature “Drift Away” by JMHBM (Johnathon M. Horner, Beat Mekanik), via Free Music Archive, under CC BY 4.0. The player illustration uses “Mathilde Fernandez - Temple Sourire (Strenx & Lezguy Edit)” with the artists’ permission. Rights to the music and artwork remain with their holders. Permission to display the demo grants visitors no additional reuse rights.

flow.title: Where the extension's data goes
flow.desc: One box, your computer, holds the dj-digger desktop app and your browser with the dj-digger extension. App and extension are joined by native messaging, their only channel. The only arrows that leave the box run from the tabs the extension opened for the app to five sites: Hypeddit, ToneDen, Bandcamp, Beatport and SoundCloud. A box for the developer stands outside with no arrow: nothing is sent there.
